learning: Compare per track with the iteration 9 baseline (215.38). Oscillation at kd 0.5 was about 0.29 at both kp 3.5 and kp 3.2, and at kd 0.3 it was 0.25. Read whether kd 0.4 lands between them on oscillation and on score. If the score falls below 213, kd 0.5 is needed and oscillation must be handled another way.
notes: Complete robot on the held iteration 8 and 9 geometry. The controller changes kd from 0.5 to 0.4 at kp 3.2 to test whether oval oscillation can fall below 0.25 while keeping most of the score gain. Iterations 7 to 9 show kp barely moves oscillation, so kd is the lever.
rationale: The Builder's geometry is the iteration 8 and 9 platform: wheel_track 0.09 m, five 12 mm sensors at x = -0.024 to +0.024 m and y = 0.04 m, mass 0.6 kg. The Integrator adopts it unchanged. Iteration 8 and 9 both ran kp 3.2 with kd 0.5 and scored 215.38. The oval steering_oscillation at that setting was 0.292, and the same value at kp 3.5 was 0.291 (iteration 7). Lowering kp from 3.5 to 3.2 therefore left oscillation essentially unchanged. The oscillation rise came from the kd change: kd 0.3 gave 0.2505 (iteration 6) and kd 0.5 gave about 0.29, while the score rose from 153 to 213. The Builder's premise that kp/wheel_track drives oscillation is not supported at this geometry. Derivative gain is the lever. This iteration keeps kp 3.2 (the best-scoring point) and sets kd to 0.4, an intermediate value between the 0.3 result (oscillation 0.25, score 153 at kp 3.5) and the 0.5 result (score 215). Expected result: oval oscillation near 0.27 or below, with the score close to 215. If the score falls well below 215, kd 0.5 was needed for the score and the next controller step should be a different damping term rather than a lower kd. Sensors, geometry, base_speed, ki and line_loss are unchanged from the 215.38 baseline.
